newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Canberra hopes to sell bulk of airports in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: Canberra hopes to sell bulk of airports in 1997/98.

text.p: Australian Finance Minister John Fahey said on Wednesday the government hoped to complete the bulk of its airport privatisation plan in 1997/98.

The governmment announced the successful bidders for Brisbane, Melbourne and Perth airports earlier on Wednesday and said it hoped to sell all others except those in Sydney in the fiscal year to June 30, 1998.

"We would hope to move early in the financial year in respect of the others and we will look at that," Fahey told reporters. "There is some considerable interest in acquiring a number of those airports."
Transport Minister John Sharp said he was unable to say when the sale of Sydney's Mascot airport and the planned second airport was likely to occur.

"The only decision we've made in regard to Sydney's Mascot airport is that we will not be making it available for sale until we, to our satisfaction, have resolved the aircraft noise problems that surround the operation of Mascot airport," Sharp said.
"It will be some time before we've reached that situation and so we will not be making a decision about Sydney airport for some time to come."
The government raised A$3.3 billion through the sale of 50-year leases for Brisbane, Melbourne and Perth airports, with an option of a further 49 years.
It was the first phase of the privatisation of more than 20 government airports in capital cities and regional centres around the country.
